About & method

This is the public face of lovhistorie, a project to reconstruct the point-in-time text of Norwegian statutes — the law as it read at any past date — as a corpus that is owned and freely publishable. Everything you read here is built only from public-domain sources.

How it's built

For each statute we start from its original enactment and replay every amendment in order, both taken from Norsk Lovtidend — the official gazette, public-domain via Nasjonalbiblioteket back to 1877 — plus the free NLOD current dumps. Replaying the amendment stream to any date yields the statute as it read on that date. The reconstruction is never shown the current official text while it runs.

Why not just use Lovdata?

The free open reconstructions seed their history with today's text as a 2001 baseline, so they are silently wrong for anything unamended by 2001. Lovdata Pro has true historical versions but is subscription-gated with reuse limits. This corpus is built from the public-domain gazette instead — owned, and correct back to 1877.

How good is it, honestly

69% of provisions on the 9-law development set reconstruct to today's official text (convergence 68.5%, as of 2026-08-21). The rest don't — and this site shows you exactly which, and how far off, via the fidelity badge and the reconstruction-vs-official comparison on every section. Reproducing a past date is scored against held-out Lovdata Pro versions internally, but that licensed text is never shown here — which is the whole reason the corpus is built from the gazette.
